source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice mcqs written from Chapter 9 (PDF 189-211), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh chapter 9 (Acid-Base Chemistry) ke poore chapter se practice MCQs hain, chapter ke sections ki tarteeb mein. Har sawal ka aik sahi jawab hai aur saath mukhtasar wajah; numerical sawalon mein hal ke qadam diye gaye hain.

blocks.prompt:
1 An acid changes the colour of litmus:
(Acid litmus ka rang kaise badalta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Acids litmus ko neele se laal karte hain; bases laal se neela (9.1).

book_ref.quote: Acids change litmus from blue to red and basic phenolphthalein from pink to colorless

blocks.prompt:
2 A base changes the colour of phenolphthalein:
(Base phenolphthalein ka rang kaise badalta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Bases phenolphthalein ko berang se gulabi (pink) karte hain (9.1).

book_ref.quote: Bases change litmus from red to blue and phenolphthalein from colorless to pink

blocks.prompt:
3 During neutralization, acids and bases react to produce ionic substances called:
(Neutralization mein acids aur bases react kar ke kaun se ionic substances banate hain?)
blocks.explanation: Neutralization (taadeel) mein acids aur bases mil kar salts (namak) banate hain (9.1).

book_ref.quote: During neutralization, acids and bases react with each other to produce ionic substances called salts

blocks.prompt:
4 Acidity in the stomach is due to excess HCl. It is treated by taking a mild base such as:
(Maide (stomach) ki acidity zyada HCl ki wajah se hoti hai. Is ka ilaaj kis halki base se hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Maide ki acidity, jo zyada HCl se hoti hai, baking soda jaisi halki bases se theek hoti hai (9.1).

book_ref.quote: Acidity in our stomachs is due to excess HCl.

blocks.prompt:
5 The main limitation of the Arrhenius theory is that it describes acid-base reactions:
(Arrhenius theory ki bari kami kya hai? Yeh acid-base reactions ko bayan karti hai:)
blocks.explanation: Arrhenius theory acid aur base ka reaction sirf aqueous (paani wale) medium mein bayan karti hai, jab ke bohat se reactions doosre solvents ya baghair solvent hote hain (9.1).

book_ref.quote: The limitations of Arrhenius theory is that it describes the reaction of an acid and base only in the aqueous medium

blocks.prompt:
6 Bronsted and Lowry independently expanded the Arrhenius theory of acids and bases in the year:
(Bronsted aur Lowry ne Arrhenius theory ko kis saal alag alag barhaya?)
blocks.explanation: 1923 mein J.N. Bronsted (Danish) aur T.M. Lowry (English) ne alag alag Arrhenius theory ko barhaya (9.1).

book_ref.quote: In 1923, the Danish chemist J.N. Bronsted and the English chemist T.M. Lowry independently expanded the Arrhenius theory

blocks.prompt:
7 According to the Bronsted-Lowry concept, an acid is a species that:
(Bronsted-Lowry concept ke mutabiq acid woh species hai jo:)

options.text: paani mein OH⁻ ions deti hai

blocks.explanation: Bronsted-Lowry acid woh species hai jo proton-transfer reaction mein proton deti hai; base proton leti hai (9.1).

book_ref.quote: an acid is the species donating a proton in a proton-transfer reaction

blocks.prompt:
8 When HCl dissolves in water, the proton transferred from HCl attaches to a lone pair on the O atom of water and forms:
(Jab HCl paani mein hal hota hai to HCl ka proton paani ke O atom ke lone pair se jur kar kya banata hai?)
blocks.explanation: HCl ka H⁺ paani ke O atom ke lone pair se jur kar hydronium ion H₃O⁺ banata hai (9.1).

book_ref.quote: where it becomes attached to a lone pair of electrons on the O atom and forms H₃O⁺

blocks.prompt:
9 The conjugate acid of water is:
(Paani ka conjugate acid kaun sa hai?)
blocks.explanation: Jab paani proton leta hai to H₃O⁺ banta hai, is liye hydronium ion paani ka conjugate acid hai (9.1).

book_ref.quote: The hydronium ion (H₃O⁺) is the conjugate acid of water.

blocks.prompt:
10 A species formed when an acid donates a proton to a base is called the:
(Jab acid base ko proton deta hai to jo species banti hai use kya kehte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Acid ke proton dene ke baad jo species bachti hai woh us ka conjugate base hai, maslan HCl se Cl⁻ (9.1).

book_ref.quote: A species formed when an acid donates a proton to a base is called the conjugate base.

blocks.prompt:
11 In the reaction NH₃(g) + H₂O(ℓ) ⇌ NH₄⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq), the species NH₄⁺ is:
(Reaction NH₃(g) + H₂O(ℓ) ⇌ NH₄⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) mein NH₄⁺ kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: NH₃ paani se proton leta hai, is liye NH₄⁺ NH₃ ka conjugate acid hai (9.1 ki book correction: yeh conjugate base nahi).

book_ref.quote: In this case, H₂O (the acid) has donated the proton and NH₃ (the base) has accepted it.

blocks.prompt:
12 Water acts as a base with HCl and as an acid with NH₃. Such a substance is called:
(Paani HCl ke saath base aur NH₃ ke saath acid ka kaam karta hai. Aisi substance ko kya kehte hain?)
blocks.explanation: H₂O amphoteric (dono khaslat wala) hai: doosre reactant ke mutabiq kabhi base aur kabhi acid ka kaam karta hai (9.1).

book_ref.quote: H₂O is amphoteric in nature because it acts as a base in one case and as an acid in the other

blocks.prompt:
13 Gaseous ammonia and HCl react without any solvent to give:
(Gas ammonia aur HCl baghair kisi solvent ke react kar ke kya banate hain?)
blocks.explanation: NH₃(g) + HCl(g) → NH₄Cl(s); Bronsted-Lowry theory aise baghair solvent ke reactions par bhi lagti hai (9.1).

book_ref.quote: The reaction between gaseous ammonia and HCl gives solid NH₄Cl.

blocks.prompt:
14 In the reaction HCl(g) + NH₃(g) → NH₄Cl(s), NH₃ is a base because it:
(Reaction HCl(g) + NH₃(g) → NH₄Cl(s) mein NH₃ base kyun hai?)

options.text: Cl⁻ ko electron pair kho deta hai

blocks.explanation: NH₃ base hai halaanke OH⁻ maujood nahi, kyun ke yeh HCl se proton leta hai (9.1).

book_ref.quote: The NH₃ acts as a base, even though hydroxide ion OH⁻ is not present

blocks.prompt:
15 According to Table 9.1, when H₂SO₄ reacts with water, the conjugate base formed is:
(Table 9.1 ke mutabiq jab H₂SO₄ paani se react karta hai to kaun sa conjugate base banta hai?)
blocks.explanation: H₂SO₄ paani ko aik proton deta hai: H₂SO₄ + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + HSO₄⁻; HSO₄⁻ conjugate base hai (Table 9.1).

book_ref.quote: Table 9.1 Conjugate Acid-Base Pairs of Common Species

blocks.prompt:
16 In the reaction H₂O + CO₃²⁻ ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + OH⁻ (Table 9.1), the conjugate acid is:
(Reaction H₂O + CO₃²⁻ ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + OH⁻ (Table 9.1) mein conjugate acid kaun sa hai?)
blocks.explanation: CO₃²⁻ base hai; yeh paani se proton le kar HCO₃⁻ banta hai jo us ka conjugate acid hai; OH⁻ paani ka conjugate base hai (Table 9.1).

book_ref.quote: Table 9.1 Conjugate Acid-Base Pairs of Common Species

blocks.text: 9.2 Lewis concept of acids and bases

blocks.prompt:
17 The generalized definition of acids and bases in terms of electron pairs was proposed by:
(Electron pairs ki bunyaad par acids aur bases ki aam definition kis ne pesh ki?)
blocks.explanation: 1923 mein G.N. Lewis ne acids aur bases ko electron pair lene ya dene ki salahiyat se define kiya (9.2).

book_ref.quote: In 1923, G.N. Lewis proposed a generalized definition of acid-base behavior

blocks.prompt:
18 A Lewis acid is any species that can:
(Lewis acid woh species hai jo:)

options.text: paani mein OH⁻ ions banati hai

blocks.explanation: Lewis acid electron pair leta hai; Lewis base electron pair deta hai (9.2).

book_ref.quote: A Lewis acid is any species (molecule or ion) that can accept a pair of electrons

blocks.prompt:
19 In a Lewis acid-base reaction, the bond formed between the acid and the base is:
(Lewis acid-base reaction mein acid aur base ke darmiyan kaun sa bond banta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Lewis acids aur bases electron pair le ya de kar coordinate covalent bond banate hain (9.2).

book_ref.quote: by their ability to accept or to donate a pair of electrons and form a coordinate covalent bond

blocks.prompt:
20 In the reaction Ag⁺ + 2NH₃ → [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺, the Lewis acid is:
(Reaction Ag⁺ + 2NH₃ → [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ mein Lewis acid kaun sa hai?)
blocks.explanation: Har NH₃ (Lewis base) electron pair musbat silver ion ko deta hai, jo Lewis acid hai (9.2).

book_ref.quote: each of two ammonia molecules, Lewis bases, donates a pair of electrons to a positively charged silver ion

blocks.prompt:
21 The charge on the adduct formed from Ag⁺ and two NH₃ molecules is:
(Ag⁺ aur do NH₃ molecules se banne wale adduct par kitna charge hai?)
blocks.explanation: Baayen taraf charges ka majmooa +1 hai (Ag⁺ + do neutral NH₃), is liye adduct par +1 hai (9.2).

book_ref.quote: The sum of charges on the left side is +1, so the acid-base adduct on the right hand side must carry a charge of +1

blocks.prompt:
22 BF₃ behaves as a very good Lewis acid because the boron atom:
(BF₃ achha Lewis acid kyun hai? Kyun ke boron atom:)

options.text: dene ke liye lone pair rakhta hai
valence shell mein sirf chhe electrons rakhta hai

blocks.explanation: BF₃ mein boron ke valence shell mein sirf chhe electrons hain (octet adhoora), is liye yeh electron pair leta hai (9.2).

book_ref.quote: The boron atom in boron trifluoride, BF₃, has only six electrons in its valence shell.

blocks.prompt:
23 In the reaction BF₃ + F⁻ → BF₄⁻, the Lewis base is:
(Reaction BF₃ + F⁻ → BF₄⁻ mein Lewis base kaun sa hai?)
blocks.explanation: Fluoride ion apna aik lone pair BF₃ ko deta hai, is liye F⁻ Lewis base hai (9.2).

book_ref.quote: a fluoride ion is the Lewis base in this reaction, donating one of its lone pairs

blocks.prompt:
24 The charge on the adduct formed when BF₃ reacts with F⁻ is:
(Jab BF₃ F⁻ se react karta hai to banne wale adduct par kitna charge hai?)
blocks.explanation: Baayen taraf charge −1 hai (BF₃ neutral, F⁻ −1), is liye adduct BF₄⁻ par bhi −1 hai (9.2).

book_ref.quote: the sum of charges on the right hand side must also be -1

blocks.prompt:
25 Pure water has a small but measurable conductance because it:
(Khalis paani ki conductance kam magar napne ke qabil kyun hai?)

options.text: is mein namak hal hote hain

blocks.explanation: Paani khud-ba-khud thora sa ionize hota hai: H₂O + H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + OH⁻, is se kuch ions bante hain (9.3).

book_ref.quote: Pure water is a poor conductor of electricity but its conductance is measurable.

blocks.prompt:
26 The molar concentration of water in pure water is about:
(Khalis paani mein paani ki molar concentration taqreeban kitni hai?)
blocks.explanation: [H₂O] = 1000 g dm⁻³ ÷ 18 g mol⁻¹ = 55.5 mol dm⁻³ (9.3).

book_ref.quote: [H₂O] in pure water may be calculated to be 1000 g dm⁻³ divided by 18 g mol⁻¹ giving 55.5 mol dm⁻³

blocks.prompt:
27 In deriving Kw, the concentration of water is taken as constant because:
(Kw nikalte waqt paani ki concentration ko constant kyun maana jata hai?)

options.text: paani bohat zyada hai aur bohat kam molecules ionize hote hain

blocks.explanation: Paani bohat zyada miqdaar mein hai aur bohat kam molecules ionize hote hain, is liye [H₂O] taqreeban constant rehti hai aur Kc ke saath mila di jati hai (9.3).

book_ref.quote: Since, water is present in very large excess and very few of its molecules undergo ionization

blocks.prompt:
28 Kw is called the:
(Kw ko kya kehte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Kw ko paani ka ionic product ya paani ka dissociation constant kehte hain (9.3).

book_ref.quote: Kw is called ionic product of water or dissociation constant of water.

blocks.prompt:
29 At 25 °C the ionic product of water is:
(25 °C par paani ka ionic product kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: Kw = Kc[H₂O] = [H⁺][OH⁻] = 25 °C par 10⁻¹⁴; Kw mein [H₂O] pehle se shamil hai (9.3 ki book correction).

book_ref.quote: The print gives Kw [H₂O] = [H⁺][OH⁻].

blocks.prompt:
30 If Kc for H₂O ⇌ H⁺ + OH⁻ were 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁶ mol dm⁻³ and [H₂O] = 55.5 mol dm⁻³, Kw = Kc[H₂O] would be:
(Agar H₂O ⇌ H⁺ + OH⁻ ka Kc 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁶ mol dm⁻³ aur [H₂O] = 55.5 mol dm⁻³ ho to Kw = Kc[H₂O] kitna hoga?)

book_ref.quote: This 1.01 x 10⁻¹⁴ is called Kw of water at 25°C.

blocks.prompt:
31 According to Table 9.2, as the temperature of water rises from 0 °C to 40 °C, Kw:
(Table 9.2 ke mutabiq paani ka temperature 0 °C se 40 °C tak barhne par Kw:)
blocks.explanation: Temperature ke saath Kw barhta hai: 0 °C par 0.11 × 10⁻¹⁴, 25 °C par 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ aur 40 °C par 3.00 × 10⁻¹⁴ (Table 9.2).

book_ref.quote: Table 9.2 Kw at various temperature.

blocks.prompt:
32 When a small amount of acid is added to pure water at 25 °C:
(Jab 25 °C par khalis paani mein thora sa acid dala jaye to:)
blocks.explanation: Acid dalne se [H⁺] > [OH⁻] ho jata hai, magar Kw wahi rehta hai, 25 °C par 10⁻¹⁴ (9.3).

book_ref.quote: In case of addition of small amount of acid.

blocks.prompt:
33 In neutral water at 25 °C, the concentration of H⁺ ions is:
(25 °C par neutral paani mein H⁺ ions ki concentration kitni hai?)
blocks.explanation: Neutral paani mein [H⁺] = [OH⁻], is liye [H⁺]² = 10⁻¹⁴ aur [H⁺] = 10⁻⁷ mol dm⁻³ (9.3).

book_ref.quote: Whenever some quantity of acid or base is added to water, then Kw remains the same

blocks.prompt:
34 The terms pH and pOH were introduced in 1909 by:
(pH aur pOH ki istilahaat 1909 mein kis ne pesh keen?)
blocks.explanation: 1909 mein Danish biochemist Sørensen ne pH aur pOH pesh kiye (9.4).

book_ref.quote: In 1909, Sørensen, a Danish biochemist, introduced the term pH and pOH.

blocks.prompt:
35 The pH and pOH scales were developed because:
(pH aur pOH scales kyun banaye gaye?)

options.text: paani mein [H⁺] hamesha sifar hota hai
har acid dalne par Kw badalta hai
[H⁺] aur [OH⁻] bohat kam hain, aasani se istemal nahi hote

blocks.explanation: Aqueous solutions mein [H⁺] aur [OH⁻] itne kam hote hain ke aasani se likhe nahi jate, is liye pH aur pOH scales banaye gaye (9.4).

book_ref.quote: the concentration of H⁺ and OH⁻ are too low to be conveniently expressed and used in calculations

blocks.prompt:
36 The pH of a solution is defined as:
(Solution ka pH kis tarah define hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: pH = −log[H⁺] aur pOH = −log[OH⁻] (9.4).

book_ref.quote: The value of pH normally varies between 0 → 14 at 25 °C.

blocks.prompt:
37 What is the pH of a solution in which [H⁺] = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³?
(Jis solution mein [H⁺] = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³ ho us ka pH kya hai?)

book_ref.quote: The value of pH normally varies between 0 → 14 at 25 °C.

blocks.prompt:
38 A solution has pOH = 4.5 at 25 °C. Its pH is:
(25 °C par aik solution ka pOH = 4.5 hai. Is ka pH kya hai?)

book_ref.quote: The pH values of some familiar aqueous solutions are shown in Figure 9.1.

blocks.prompt:
39 The pH of a solution is 5.6. The [H⁺] of the solution is about:
(Aik solution ka pH 5.6 hai. Is ki [H⁺] taqreeban kitni hai?)
blocks.explanation: [H⁺] = 10⁻ᵖᴴ = 10⁻⁵·⁶ = 2.5 × 10⁻⁶ mol dm⁻³ (Sample Problem 9.1 ka tareeqa; pH se [H⁺] milta hai).

book_ref.quote: Calculate the pOH from the pH: pOH = 14 − pH; pOH = 14 − 9.2; pOH = 4.8

blocks.prompt:
40 A solution has pH 3.4 at 25 °C. Its [OH⁻] is about:
(25 °C par aik solution ka pH 3.4 hai. Is ki [OH⁻] taqreeban kitni hai?)

book_ref.quote: The pH gives the H⁺ concentration, not OH⁻

blocks.prompt:
41 At 25 °C a solution has [H⁺] = 2.0 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³. Using Kw = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴, its [OH⁻] is:
(25 °C par aik solution mein [H⁺] = 2.0 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ hai. Kw = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ se [OH⁻] kitni hai?)
blocks.explanation: [OH⁻] = Kw/[H⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ / 2.0 × 10⁻⁵ = 5.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ mol dm⁻³ (Sample Problem 9.2 ka tareeqa).

book_ref.quote: Substitute the known values of Kw and the concentration of H⁺

blocks.prompt:
42 A solution with [OH⁻] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³ at 25 °C has pH:
(25 °C par jis solution mein [OH⁻] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³ ho us ka pH kya hai?)

book_ref.quote: The value of pH normally varies between 0 → 14 at 25 °C.

blocks.prompt:
43 Which statement about pH values is correct according to the chapter?
(Chapter ke mutabiq pH ke baare mein kaun sa bayan durust hai?)

options.text: pH kabhi 0 se kam nahi hota
Manfi pH aur 14 se zyada pH wale solutions bhi maloom hain
pH kabhi 7 se zyada nahi hota
har acid ka pH theek 1 hota hai

blocks.explanation: 25 °C par pH aam tor par 0 se 14 ke darmiyan hota hai, magar manfi (negative) pH aur 14 se zyada pH wale solutions bhi maloom hain (9.4).

book_ref.quote: Solutions of negative pH and having values more than 14 are also known.

blocks.prompt:
44 For neutral water at 25 °C, the values of pH and pOH are:
(25 °C par neutral paani ke pH aur pOH kya hain?)
blocks.explanation: Neutral paani ke liye pH = −log(10⁻⁷) = 7 aur pOH = 7; pH + pOH = 14 (9.4).

book_ref.quote: These two quantities can be calculated as:

blocks.prompt:
45 The quantitative measure of the strength of an acid is its:
(Acid ki taqat (strength) ka miqdaari paimana kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Ka, yani acid ka dissociation constant, acid ki taqat ka miqdaari paimana hai (9.5).

book_ref.quote: is the quantitative measure of the strength of the acid

blocks.prompt:
46 Many acids are weak electrolytes. This means they:
(Bohat se acids weak electrolytes hain. Is ka matlab hai ke woh:)

options.text: 100% se bohat kam ionize hote hain

blocks.explanation: Weak acids 100% se bohat kam ionize hote hain (9.5).

book_ref.quote: Many acids are weak electrolytes and ionize to an extent which is much less than 100%.

blocks.prompt:
47 An acid with Ka = 5 × 10⁻² is classified in the chapter as:
(Jis acid ka Ka = 5 × 10⁻² ho use chapter mein kya kaha gaya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Ka 1 se 10⁻³ ke darmiyan ho to acid moderately strong hai; 5 × 10⁻² isi range mein hai (9.5).

book_ref.quote: Ka = 1 to 10⁻³ acid is moderately strong.

blocks.prompt:
48 Acetic acid has Ka = 1.85 × 10⁻⁵. It is therefore:
(Acetic acid ka Ka = 1.85 × 10⁻⁵ hai. Is liye yeh:)
blocks.explanation: Ka < 10⁻³ ho to acid weak hai; acetic acid ka 1.85 × 10⁻⁵ hai, is liye weak (9.5).

book_ref.quote: When Ka < 10⁻³ acid is weak.

blocks.prompt:
49 An acid is classified as strong when its Ka is:
(Acid ko strong kab kaha jata hai? Jab us ka Ka:)
blocks.explanation: Ka > 1 ho to acid strong hai (9.5).

book_ref.quote: Acids and bases, when dissolved in water, may or may not be completely dissociated.

blocks.prompt:
50 In deriving Ka for HA + H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + A⁻, Ka is equal to:
(HA + H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + A⁻ ke liye Ka nikalte waqt Ka kis ke barabar hai?)
blocks.explanation: Kc[H₂O] = [H₃O⁺][A⁻]/[HA]; is constant Kc[H₂O] ko Ka kehte hain (9.5).

book_ref.quote: Kc for the reversible reaction will be written as follows:

blocks.prompt:
51 From Table 9.3, which of these acids is the weakest: CH₃COOH (1.85 × 10⁻⁵), H₂CO₃ (4.4 × 10⁻⁷), H₂S (1.0 × 10⁻⁷) or NH₄⁺ (5.7 × 10⁻¹⁰)?
(Table 9.3 se in mein sab se weak acid kaun sa hai: CH₃COOH (1.85 × 10⁻⁵), H₂CO₃ (4.4 × 10⁻⁷), H₂S (1.0 × 10⁻⁷) ya NH₄⁺ (5.7 × 10⁻¹⁰)?)
blocks.explanation: Ka jitna chhota, acid utna weak; NH₄⁺ ka Ka sab se chhota, 5.7 × 10⁻¹⁰ hai (Table 9.3).

book_ref.quote: Table 9.3 The values of Ka for some acids

blocks.prompt:
52 For a weak acid, [H₃O⁺] is not equal to the initial concentration of the acid because:
(Weak acid mein [H₃O⁺] acid ki shuru ki concentration ke barabar kyun nahi hoti?)

options.text: acid poori tarah dissociate nahi hota
acid poori tarah dissociate hota hai
H₃O⁺ A⁻ se poora react kar leta hai

blocks.explanation: Weak acids poori tarah dissociate nahi hote, is liye [H₃O⁺] equilibrium expression se nikalte hain (9.5.1).

book_ref.quote: The weak acids do not completely dissociate in water.

blocks.prompt:
53 For a weak acid of concentration C, the approximation C − x ≈ C is used because:
(Concentration C wale weak acid ke liye C − x ≈ C kyun liya jata hai?)

options.text: x, C ke muqable mein bohat chhota hai

blocks.explanation: Weak acids mein x aam tor par C ke muqable mein bohat chhota hota hai, is liye Ka ≈ x²/C (9.5.1).

book_ref.quote: For weak acids, x is usually very small compared to C, so C – x ≈ C.

blocks.prompt:
54 For a weak acid HA of concentration C, [H₃O⁺] is approximately:
(Concentration C wale weak acid HA ke liye [H₃O⁺] taqreeban kitni hai?)
blocks.explanation: Ka ≈ x²/C, is liye x = [H₃O⁺] ≈ √(Ka × C) (9.5.1).

book_ref.quote: Thus, the concentration of H₃O⁺ is given by:

blocks.prompt:
55 The [H₃O⁺] in a 0.05 mol dm⁻³ acetic acid solution (Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵) is about:
(0.05 mol dm⁻³ acetic acid solution (Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵) mein [H₃O⁺] taqreeban kitni hai?)

book_ref.quote: The concentration [H₃O⁺] in the solution is approximately 1.34 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³.

blocks.prompt:
56 A weak acid HA has Ka = 4.0 × 10⁻⁶. In a 0.01 mol dm⁻³ solution, [H₃O⁺] is about:
(Aik weak acid HA ka Ka = 4.0 × 10⁻⁶ hai. 0.01 mol dm⁻³ solution mein [H₃O⁺] taqreeban kitni hai?)

book_ref.quote: So, the equilibrium expression is used to calculate the H₃O⁺ concentration.

blocks.prompt:
57 A 0.10 mol dm⁻³ solution of a weak acid HA has pH = 3.0. Its Ka is about:
(Weak acid HA ke 0.10 mol dm⁻³ solution ka pH = 3.0 hai. Is ka Ka taqreeban kitna hai?)

book_ref.quote: This equation can be used to calculate Ka for any acidic solution if we know the pH or [H⁺] of that solution

blocks.prompt:
58 The suppression of ionization of a weak electrolyte by adding a common ion is called:
(Weak electrolyte mein common ion dal kar us ki ionization ko dabane ko kya kehte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Yeh common ion effect ki definition hai (9.6).

book_ref.quote: The suppression of ionization of a weak electrolyte by adding a common ion to it is called common ion effect.

blocks.prompt:
59 Sodium chloride is purified by passing HCl gas through:
(Sodium chloride ko saaf karne ke liye HCl gas kis mein se guzari jati hai?)
blocks.explanation: NaCl ko brine (NaCl ka saturated solution) mein HCl gas guzaar kar saaf kiya jata hai (9.6).

book_ref.quote: We are familiar with purification of sodium chloride by passing hydrogen chloride gas through brine

blocks.prompt:
60 On passing HCl gas through brine, NaCl crystallizes out because:
(Brine mein HCl gas guzarne par NaCl ke crystals kyun nikal aate hain?)

options.text: [Cl⁻] barhti hai aur equilibrium constant qaim rakhne ke liye NaCl alag hota hai
HCl Na⁺ se NaH banata hai
brine ka temperature tezi se barhta hai
